item.text: I’ll enable Chrome Safe Browsing at the browser policy level so it applies reliably, then verify the policy file is in place.

Chrome is installed as Google Chrome, and there are no existing managed Chrome policy files. I’m going to add a small managed policy that turns Safe Browsing on without changing unrelated Chrome settings.

item.command: /bin/bash -lc 'sudo install -d -m 755 /etc/opt/chrome/policies/managed && sudo install -m 644 /home/user/tmp/chrome-safe-browsing-policy.json /etc/opt/chrome/policies/managed/safe-browsing.json && sudo rm -f /home/user/tmp/chrome-safe-browsing-policy.json && sudo cat /etc/opt/chrome/policies/managed/safe-browsing.json'

item.text: The managed policy is now installed. I’m checking the current profile preference too, so the visible Chrome setting aligns with the policy instead of waiting on defaults.

The profile currently has Safe Browsing turned off, so I’m going to close Chrome gracefully, update that preference, and relaunch it. The managed policy will also keep the protection enabled afterward.

item.command: /bin/bash -lc 'tmp=$(mktemp) && jq '"'.safebrowsing.enabled = true | .safebrowsing.enhanced = false' /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences > \""'$tmp" && install -m 600 "$tmp" /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences && rm -f "$tmp" && jq '"'.safebrowsing' /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences"
